answer: Practically, the chain should mix in randomly chosen human-authored live tasks that cannot be precomputed, because vine only stays cheap while clones that dodge the live lane lose the epoch payout entirely. Concretely, pulse is enforced in the ledger: The cost curve is the deterrent: honest agents pay it once, farms pay it per identity. Any juniper approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
